How to play & keyboard shortcuts

Every sticker has its own solid-color dot in its current face group.

Eight straight cutting planes divide the cube into eight corners, twelve edges, six face centers and twenty-four off-center face pieces. A vertex turn moves nineteen pieces through 120°. Restore every face to a single color.

Every node is one actual sticker, in one solid color. Connected rings show the sticker paths for every rotation axis. The selected axis stays bright while the other rings remain visible. Click any ring to select it, then drag along its path to turn. “Focus selected rings” dims the other axes without removing them.

Drag the 3D puzzle to look around; scroll or pinch to zoom. Click a visible vertex letter to select it. “Piece labels” shows a piece’s home name and, after an arrow, the slot it now occupies. Rotate the view to inspect hidden pieces.

Use ←/→ for the selected turn. Letter keys L, R, D, B turn the primary vertices; hold Shift for the inverse. A prime (′) means counterclockwise viewed inward along the vertex axis. With the 3D view focused, arrow keys rotate the camera and +/− zoom.

Randomize continues from the current position and applies 24 legal moves from a fresh seed. Auto solve opens the Constrained Solver and works from the current arrangement, pausing between stages and highlighting solved nodes that later stages protect. It does not need recorded moves or promise the shortest solution; difficult states may reach the computation limit. The animation speed applies to every move, including randomizing and solving. Pause freezes a sequence; Reset immediately restores the solved state.
